newsitem.title: ITALY: S&P puts BancoNapoli 'B' rating on Creditwatch.
newsitem.headline: S&P puts BancoNapoli 'B' rating on Creditwatch.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said it placed on Creditwatch with positive implications its single 'B' short-term rating on the counterparty obligations of Banco di Napoli SpA, and US commercial paper programme of BdN Commercial Paper U.S.A. Inc, guaranteed by Banco di Napoli SpA, following the issue of an Italian government decree outlining procedures for the privatisation of the bank.

S&P said in a statement received in Milan that the rating was lowered on August 2, 1995 to reflect the fragile financial position of the bank and the uncertainty regarding the timeliness of its recapitalisation.
At the end of July this year the Italian government announced a comprehensive rescue plan aiming at the bank's privatisation by the end of 1996.
A thorough reorganisation of the bank is being implemented, aimed at improving risk management and cost control, as well as relaunching commercial operations.
"Standard & Poor's views positively the strategy designed by the new management team, which addresses the bank's fundamental weaknesses," the statement said.
S&P noted that the rescue package still has to be approved by the Italian parliament and the European Commission.

"The Creditwatch resolution also will depend on clarification regarding the mechanics of the special vehicle that will receive Banco di Napoli's impaired assets, on profitability prospects for the bank and on the level of support that could be expected from the new shareholder of the bank after the privatisation," S&P added.
